clue.text: Statements that could mean life or death

definitions.meaning: declarations or assertions put into words
a judge's verdict of punishment might be life imprisonment or execution

explanation.surface: Words whose consequences are grave, perhaps spoken in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on courtroom penalties: a life term or the death penalty is what a judge passes.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammatical units expressing a statement and the punishments passed by judges share one word.

clue.text: Island of saint and prophet

parts.note: Amos is an Old Testament prophet

explanation.surface: An island associated with a holy man and a seer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek isle in the Aegean.

clue.text: Good backing with such discs?

parts.note: a healthy spine has spinal discs that stay in place rather than slipping

explanation.surface: Recording music with good support from records.
explanation.walkthrough: Discs suggest records; they are spinal discs, and a good back has none that are slipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that resists sliding, like a spine whose discs stay put.

clue.text: Men who cure afflictions of the spirit

definitions.text: Men who cure afflictions of the spirit

parts.words: Men who cure afflictions of the spirit
parts.note: people who drive out possessing demons, so an affliction caused by a spirit

explanation.surface: Psychiatrists who treat troubled minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afflictions of the spirit' suggests mental troubles; it means possession by a spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Priests who expel demons from the possessed.

clue.text: Island doctor, well-bred, is worldly in outlook

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island
MO is a medical officer, a doctor
polite means courteous, well-bred

explanation.surface: A refined island physician has a broad view of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a noun, a citizen of the world, so read the definition as one who is worldly in outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the world, a person at home in many countries and cultures.

clue.text: Stand in for journalist

explanation.surface: Deputize for a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for substitute and for sub-editor, a newspaper role.

clue.text: Ray's rendezvous with others at such a point

definitions.text: Ray's rendezvous with others at such a point

parts.words: Ray's rendezvous with others at such a point
parts.note: in optics, light beams converge at one particular spot after a lens; Ray reads as a man's name meeting friends

explanation.surface: A man named Ray arranges to meet his friends at a particular place.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray looks like a person's name, but it is a beam of light; lenses bring beams together at one spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Light beams meet at a lens's convergence spot, which optics names with this adjective.

clue.text: Once formed by military boundaries

definitions.meaning: soldiers once drilled by forming ranks of four
in cricket, a ball reaching the rope along the ground scores four runs

explanation.surface: Something once shaped by army borders.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's boundary hits score four runs; old drill orders told soldiers to form ranks in this way.
explanation.definitionFit: An old drill formation of ranks, and cricket scoring shots worth that many runs.

clue.text: Tom gets no bridge in SE London

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a ford is a river crossing where there is no bridge

explanation.surface: A man called Tom finds no bridge in south-east London.
explanation.walkthrough: Catford is a district of south-east London.
explanation.definitionFit: A district in the south-east of the capital.

clue.text: Regions that are highest near the poles

definitions.meaning: areas or zones of the earth

definitions.text: that are highest near the poles
definitions.meaning: angular distance from the equator reaches ninety degrees at either pole

explanation.surface: Areas whose height peaks close to the ends of the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Zones of the globe, and the angular measures from the equator which peak at the poles.

clue.text: Island tries fruit

parts.note: the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea
has a go, so goes means tries

explanation.surface: Someone on an island has a go at some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropical stone fruits with orange flesh, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Note high-class title organized for flyer

parts.note: B is a note in the musical scale

indicators.note: organized says the letters are arranged into a new order

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A memo about an upper-class title being arranged, perhaps for a leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organized' is the anagram signal for U plus the clue word title. 'flyer' suggests a leaflet but means a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small blue and yellow garden bird, and birds are creatures that fly.

clue.text: This law confuses Alice somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A complicated piece of law baffles a girl called Alice.
explanation.walkthrough: The Salic law was the Frankish code barring women from inheriting the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: A Frankish legal code excluding females from royal succession is a statute of that name.

clue.text: Source of smell at plant located underground

definitions.meaning: the fragrant rootstock of an iris used in perfumes
the buried part of an iris plant, its rhizome

explanation.surface: Finding where a smell comes from at a plant buried below ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The violet-scented iris rhizome is used in perfumery and is the buried part of the plant.

clue.text: Second chance to retrieve lost tie ?

definitions.text: Second chance to retrieve lost tie

parts.words: Second chance to retrieve lost tie
parts.note: a repeat fixture lets a team avenge a defeat in a cup game

explanation.surface: An opportunity to recover a missing necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie' looks like neckwear but is a sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A rematch gives a beaten side another go at a fixture.

clue.text: Worm fatal to Egypt

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for a snake or serpent
Egypt stands for Cleopatra, killed by a snakebite in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A parasite that proved deadly to a whole country.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Cleopatra is addressed as 'Egypt' and calls the snake that kills her a worm.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra died from the bite of a venomous Egyptian snake, which Shakespeare calls a worm.

clue.text: Unusually cool. Paris is a stronghold of classical urbanity

indicators.note: unusually says the letters appear in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: The French capital is surprisingly chilly yet a fortress of refined civility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges COOL and PARIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The citadel of an ancient Greek city, especially Athens, a fortress of classical civilisation.

clue.text: Writing quickly to editor, I having staff-vacancies

parts.note: shorthand is a system of rapid writing

explanation.surface: A boss short of staff dictates quickly to the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short of workers is lacking hands, a firm undermanned.

clue.text: The talked-about band-leader?

parts.note: Irving Berlin's song about a ragtime band asks listeners to come and hear its leader

explanation.surface: A celebrated conductor of a band.
explanation.walkthrough: Berlin's song 'Alexander's Ragtime Band' made its leader much talked about.
explanation.definitionFit: The bandleader named in Irving Berlin's ragtime song.

clue.text: Dresses. French stone for revolutionary leader

parts.note: robes are dresses or gowns
pierre is the French word for stone

explanation.surface: Clothing and French masonry linked with a radical figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Robespierre led the Jacobins during the French Revolution's Terror.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jacobin who led the Terror during the French Revolution.

clue.text: Typical of human understanding.

parts.note: read as under-standing, what humans stand on: two feet

explanation.surface: Characteristic of human comprehension.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'understanding' as what is under standing humans: two feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking on two feet is a characteristic of people.

clue.text: Short puffs

parts.note: a puff is a promotional notice, and the clipped form of advertisements is what is wanted

explanation.surface: Brief breaths of air or smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: Puffs here are promotional plugs, not breaths; 'Short' asks for the abbreviated word for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotional plugs are advertisements, and the clipped form of that word is wanted.

clue.text: Publicize row with top travel company?

parts.note: to air an issue is to publicize it
a line is a row

explanation.surface: Announce a dispute with a leading tour firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' hints that this company travels up above, in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrier offering flights is a travel firm whose journeys are overhead.

clue.text: Opium addict's vain hope

parts.note: a fantasy imagined while smoking an opium pipe, now any unrealistic wish

explanation.surface: A drug user's empty longing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase for an unrealistic fantasy began with the visions of opium smokers.

clue.text: Food programmes for conferences

definitions.meaning: a diet is a formal assembly, as in the Diet of Worms

explanation.surface: Cookery shows for conventions.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating regimes, and formal assemblies such as the Diet of Worms.

clue.text: March past she follows in Paris

definitions.text: March past she follows in Paris

parts.words: March past she follows in Paris
parts.note: in French the month that comes after March, which is also a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman follows a military parade in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March past' looks like a parade; read it as after the month of March, in French; the word is also a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The French name for the month after March, also used as a girl's name.

clue.text: Crookedly try conversions of capital in W. Africa

indicators.note: crookedly says the letters are put out of line

parts.note: in rugby, converting a try by kicking is scoring goals

explanation.surface: Kicking rugby conversions badly in a West African capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crookedly' rearranges GOALS, a rugby conversion being a goal kicked after a try. Lagos was Nigeria's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The former capital of Nigeria, in West Africa.

clue.text: Greek interpreter authorized to work with Scott ?

definitions.text: Greek interpreter authorized to work with Scott

parts.words: Greek interpreter authorized to work with Scott
parts.note: the Greek-English Lexicon is known by the names of its two compilers, the second being Scott

explanation.surface: A translator from Greek licensed to collaborate with someone called Scott.
explanation.walkthrough: Liddell and Scott is the standard Greek-English Lexicon; Henry Liddell was Alice Liddell's father.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Liddell compiled the standard Greek lexicon with Robert Scott, so he interprets Greek.

clue.text: Look round for a game of cards

parts.note: lo is an old word for look; that these letters also start the clue word is a coincidence
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Searching around for a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: An old card game with forfeits paid into a pool.

clue.text: Haymaking could put on weight on the Thames

definitions.text: Haymaking could put on weight on the Thames

parts.words: Haymaking could put on weight on the Thames
parts.note: the word for spreading hay to dry, with TON, a weight, added becomes ..., a riverside place

explanation.surface: Farm work that might make someone heavier beside the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Haymaking is the definition; adding TON, a weight, gives Teddington, a town on the Thames in south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning and spreading mown grass to dry is a stage of haymaking.

clue.text: Leading barmen

parts.note: bar men are barristers, and senior ones, King's or Queen's Counsel, wear gowns of a fine fabric

explanation.surface: Head bartenders.
explanation.walkthrough: Barmen suggests pub staff; here they are members of the Bar, whose senior counsel take a fine-fabric gown.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior barristers wear gowns of a fine fabric, and the fabric names them.

clue.text: Difference achieved by Hortense's make-up

indicators.note: make-up as a verb phrase says the letters are composed afresh

parts.note: the name with its possessive S counted as a letter

explanation.surface: A distinction brought about by a woman's cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' rearranges HORTENSES; 'make-up' looks like cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Being distinct or separate from others is a state of difference.
